stories.headline: Pentagon says Fort Hood shooter Nidal Hasan’s Dec. 3 firing-squad execution will be livestreamed after Hegseth vows it will be ‘public’
stories.summary: The Pentagon said Thursday that the firing-squad execution of Fort Hood shooter Nidal Malik Hasan will be livestreamed, after Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said the execution would be public. “We’ll make sure that people are able to watch it, that it’s public,” Hegseth told Real America’s Voice in an interview aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln on Wednesday, confirming the execution will take place at Fort Hood on Dec. 3. Asked whether Hasan had made any final requests or reached out to the administration, Hegseth replied: “Don’t care. We’ll see him on December 3rd.” Pentagon officials said more details would follow, and the White House referred questions about the livestream to the Pentagon. Hasan, a former Army psychiatrist, killed 13 people and wounded 32 in the 2009 attack on the Texas base; President Trump approved his execution last week. Hegseth said the military has not carried out a firing-squad execution since World War II; the AP notes the last U.S. military execution of any kind was the April 1961 hanging of Army Pvt. John Bennett.

stories.headline: Trump hands Elon Musk the National Medal of Science and calls him ‘our modern-day Thomas Edison’ — then receives his late uncle’s Reagan-era medal
stories.summary: President Trump presented the nation’s top science and technology honors Thursday at a “golden age” of science ceremony, giving the National Medal of Science to SpaceX and Tesla CEO Elon Musk, Nvidia’s Jensen Huang, Google co-founder Sergey Brin and AMD’s Lisa Su, and the National Medal of Technology and Innovation to Dell CEO Michael Dell and Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella. He saved his warmest words for Musk, a year after their public blowup: calling him “my friend” and a “national treasure,” Trump said “there is nobody like him” and “Elon is our modern-day Thomas Edison.” None of the CEOs spoke; they accepted gold medals the president handed over in jewelry boxes, and he praised Dell and his wife, Susan, who gave $250 million to the Trump Accounts program, as “unbelievable philanthropists.” The ceremony also played a tribute to Trump’s uncle, MIT physicist Dr. John Trump, who helped develop wartime radar, was asked by the FBI to examine Nikola Tesla’s papers after Tesla’s death in 1943, and received the National Medal of Science from Ronald Reagan in 1983. The president was given that framed medal, with its Reagan-signed certificate, calling it the honor of his uncle’s lifetime.

stories.headline: Trumbull police say a Bridgeport man burglarized a Beardsley Parkway day care overnight, took $1,200 and the owner’s car — and was caught at the wheel in Bridgeport
stories.summary: Trumbull Police posted details Thursday of the arrest of Latrell Eppes, 32, of Bridgeport, in a burglary at a day care facility on Beardsley Parkway. According to the department, the day care’s owner called police around 7:15 a.m. to report that the business had been entered overnight and about $1,200 in cash was stolen, and that a car was also missing. While officers were investigating, the vehicle was tracked to the parking lot of the North End Variety store in Bridgeport, where officers found Eppes walking out of the store and getting into the car and took him into custody without incident. Police say he had a large amount of cash, suspected narcotics, the keys to the stolen vehicle and cash believed to have come from the day care. Eppes was charged with burglary, larceny of a motor vehicle, possession of narcotics and related offenses and was held on a $50,000 bond. The town’s release dates the arrest to Sunday, Sept. 20, with a court appearance that was set for Sept. 30.

stories.headline: Apple’s second October launch: touchscreen OLED MacBook Pros with a Dynamic Island and an OLED iPad mini are reportedly coming around Oct. 27
stories.summary: Apple will introduce new touchscreen MacBook Pro models with OLED displays, plus an OLED iPad mini, “on or around” Tuesday, Oct. 27, MacRumors reports, citing Bloomberg; the launch is also expected to include an M6 14-inch MacBook Pro and an M6 iMac. It follows Apple’s Oct. 13 “Welcome home” launch of a new smart-home hub, a revamped Apple TV 4K and a refreshed HomePod mini, and both launches are expected to include an online video presentation and hands-on time for the press. Apple has been working on an OLED MacBook for years, and while some rumors suggested a “MacBook Ultra” name, Bloomberg says the 14- and 16-inch machines will stay in the MacBook Pro family — thinner and lighter than today’s models, with OLED touchscreens and a Dynamic Island. The new iPad mini is said to get a landscape front camera for video calls, a redesigned speaker system and its first OLED display.

stories.headline: Godox’s $85 magnetic A2 snaps onto an iPhone and brings back a real xenon flash, with TTL, 1/8000s sync and a bi-color video light
stories.summary: Godox has launched the Smartphone Xenon Flash A2, a MagSafe-mounted strobe aimed at the current craze for the look of a real camera flash, which has young shooters buying old point-and-shoots. It works with the iPhone 15 series and newer, including the iPhone Air, with Android and HarmonyOS support in development. The flash has a guide number of about 15 (ISO 100, meters), so it is meant for subjects within about two meters, and syncs at shutter speeds up to 1/8000s; Godox says a coming smartphone wireless trigger will let it fire the company’s speedlights and outdoor strobes for more power. For video it adds a 3-watt bi-color LED adjustable from 2800K to 6000K. Setup uses an NFC scan and Godox’s camera app, with an Auto TTL mode, Natural, Even and Contrast effects, and manual shutter and flash control; it can be used on the phone or detached over Bluetooth, mounted on anything magnetic, and paired with bounce cards, a snoot and honeycomb. PetaPixel notes it picks up the idea of Profoto’s discontinued C1. The 93-gram A2 comes in white, silver, burgundy and black and is on preorder for $84.90.

stories.headline: Slash receives the 2026 Les Paul Spirit Award — carved from Les Paul’s own hand-built studio boards — and remembers jamming with the inventor
stories.summary: Guns N’ Roses guitarist Slash received the 2026 Les Paul Spirit Award on Monday, Oct. 5, at a private celebration at the Les Paul Recording Studio at Universal Master Recordings in Hollywood, presented by the Les Paul Foundation with Gibson Gives, Gibson’s philanthropic arm. The award itself was made from hand-carved acoustic boards Les Paul built and used in his home recording studio, so no two are alike. Slash, who was friends with Paul and often played with him, said Paul “was so much more than a great guitarist and innovator. He was an actual inventor who changed the instrument itself, built groundbreaking recording equipment and completely reimagined how artists could record music,” and called the honor “tremendous.” Foundation executive director Michael Braunstein said that if Paul were alive, “Slash and he would be jamming onstage together somewhere regularly.” Previous recipients include Bob Weir, Nile Rodgers, The Edge, Peter Frampton and Steve Miller. Blabbermouth adds that Slash plans a new album with Myles Kennedy and the Conspirators in February, followed by a solo tour in April.

stories.headline: Babylon Bee: ‘Aaron Rodgers Gives Up Ayahuasca After Getting Sacked By Big Bird’
stories.summary: In the Babylon Bee’s latest sports satire, Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers decides to quit the psychedelic ayahuasca after being sacked on third down by “the gargantuan yellow form of Big Bird,” who beat the left tackle “with an incredible swim move” and put the running back “on skates with a quick spin.” “He bodied me, man,” the fictional Rodgers says. “It was like I was in an explosion of pain and yellow feathers.” Teammates in the piece report the pocket was clean and no defender was anywhere near him — right guard Brock Hoffman says Rodgers just hit the turf screaming “No, Big Bird!” and then warned him, “Stay away from me, Elmo. You and your red demon hands!” The story ends with Rodgers asking stadium security to remove the Count for gleefully tallying his interceptions.

stories.headline: Vance cuts Microsoft, Adobe and the big IT outsourcers out of the green-card pipeline for H-1B workers, saying they passed over Americans
stories.summary: The Trump administration on Thursday suspended Microsoft, Adobe and IT outsourcing firms Cognizant, Infosys, Tata Consultancy Services, Wipro, HCL Technologies and Capgemini from the permanent labor certification program that lets employers sponsor H-1B visa holders for green cards. “We will not accept any new or process any pending permanent labor certification applications involving these companies,” Labor Secretary Keith Sonderling said. Vice President JD Vance, announcing the move, accused the companies of deliberately under-advertising jobs at home so they could hire from abroad, using the lack of response “to then go and replace American workers with what is effectively foreign indentured servants,” and said no company “has used this system more than Microsoft.” Microsoft answered that most of its U.S. employees are Americans, that 80 percent of its roughly 6,000 H-1B filings last fiscal year were extensions or status changes for existing staff, and that new hires on the visas equal only 1 percent of its U.S. workforce. Engadget notes the Justice Department won a $3.2 million settlement from OpenAI in August over similar under-advertising claims, after earlier cases against Meta and Apple, and that the government is also investigating nine universities, including Harvard, Yale and Stanford, over alleged J-1 visa abuses.

stories.headline: USS Abraham Lincoln comes home to San Diego after a record 265 straight days at sea — with a Presidential Unit Citation for 3,693 combat missions against Iran
stories.summary: The aircraft carrier USS Abraham Lincoln returned to San Diego on Thursday after supporting the war against Iran on a record-setting deployment that included 265 uninterrupted days at sea. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth flew out to the ship Wednesday to award the crew the Presidential Unit Citation, the highest honor a unit can receive, and pushed back on efforts to turn the Lincoln into “a symbol of dysfunction or a symbol of low morale or a symbol of a failed mission,” telling sailors President Trump “couldn’t be more proud of what you executed.” According to the citation, the Lincoln and its strike group flew 3,693 combat missions, delivered 1.37 million pounds of ordnance, launched 450 Tomahawk cruise missiles, shot down 77 one-way attack drones and sank 64 Iranian warships. The carrier left San Diego in November and drew national attention over reports of crew stress and food and hygiene shortages; the Navy later acknowledged meal options were briefly cut from two to one, and told lawmakers eight sailors attempted suicide during the deployment, a number experts call low for a 6,000-sailor strike group. The crew got its first port call, in Thailand, early last month after the USS George Washington relieved it in August.

stories.headline: New indictment charges Maduro and his wife with conspiring to torture more than a dozen Americans — electric shock, beatings and forced injections
stories.summary: Federal prosecutors in Manhattan filed a superseding indictment Thursday adding a charge of conspiracy to commit torture against deposed Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro and his wife, Cilia Flores, who were already charged with narco-terrorism conspiracy, cocaine importation conspiracy and machine-gun and destructive-device counts. “The Maduro regime subjected over a dozen American citizens to torture while held in custody of the Venezuelan government — including drugs, electrocution, sexual assault, and more,” FBI Director Kash Patel said. The 30-page indictment says Maduro ordered opponents detained and tortured, received regular updates on interrogations and, about one defiant prisoner, told officials to “squeeze them harder”; it says one American arrested in 2022 was given injections that caused seizures, and a U.S. citizen held in 2023 was told he was being kept alive because his citizenship made him useful in a prisoner swap. At a hearing Thursday, Judge Henry J. Ricardo denied bail for Flores, who cited heart problems, noting her access to “considerable funds,” and allowed her arraignment on the new charge to be delayed. The couple, brought to the U.S. by the military to face the January indictment, have pleaded not guilty to the original charges.

stories.headline: Isaias knocks nearly two-thirds of Gulf oil output offline as it rapidly strengthens toward landfall — and analysts warn there’s ‘no slack in the system’ for gas prices
stories.summary: Hurricane Isaias is rapidly intensifying in the Gulf of Mexico and is expected to make landfall on the northeastern Gulf shore late Friday or early Saturday, and it is already squeezing U.S. energy supplies. By noon Thursday, nearly two-thirds of Gulf oil production and 57% of natural gas production had been shut in, NBC News reports, with Chevron shutting four of its Gulf assets and Shell halting production at five sites. Andy Lipow of Lipow Oil Associates said nearly all U.S. offshore production and about 14% of the nation’s refining capacity sit in the storm’s path, and with refineries already running flat out, “there is no slack in the system”; GasBuddy’s Patrick De Haan said flooded refineries could be offline for up to 10 days, producing a short-term squeeze at the pump. The national average was $4.36 a gallon Thursday, up 21 cents over the past month, and Brent crude jumped nearly 5% in early trading on reports President Trump was weighing renewed strikes on Iran. De Haan said the bigger long-term worry is Ukraine’s attacks on Russian refineries, which he expects to keep pressure on fuel for three to six months.

stories.headline: Trump-appointed judge presses the DOJ on its White House ban of CNN, MS NOW and Politico — and keeps their reporters inside until he rules by Tuesday
stories.summary: Lawyers for CNN, MS NOW and Politico were back before U.S. District Judge Timothy Kelly on Thursday seeking a preliminary injunction against President Trump’s ban on their reporters, which they say affects 78 credentialed journalists. The Justice Department’s Michael Velchik argued the president determined the outlets’ reporters failed to meet minimum professional journalistic standards and published articles that put national security at risk, while the outlets’ lawyer, Ted Boutrous, said Trump had made clear the ban was about coverage he dislikes and that he “got up on the wrong side of the bed.” Kelly, a Trump appointee, was skeptical, saying the president “seems to have said publicly and on several occasions” he acted “because of X and Y, and now the government is coming to court saying no, it was actually Z,” and calling due process “probably the biggest hurdle” for the government, citing a 2020 D.C. Circuit ruling that the White House must give fair notice and meaningful standards before suspending a credential. His temporary restraining order, set to expire Thursday, now runs through Tuesday, so the three outlets keep White House access into next week; he said he will rule on the injunction no later than Tuesday.

stories.headline: Trumbull’s Rep. David Rutigliano makes his 123rd District case: give state surpluses back to taxpayers, rethink energy deregulation and end ‘one party rule’ in Hartford
stories.summary: Patch Trumbull posted incumbent state Rep. David Rutigliano’s candidate questionnaire Thursday morning, a day after it ran Democratic challenger Bill Mecca’s, ahead of the Nov. 3 election for the 123rd House District. Rutigliano, 60, a Republican chef and restaurateur who previously served on Trumbull’s Board of Finance and Economic Development Commission says “Hartford is out of balance” and “overwhelming one party rule has not served us well.” He names affordability as the state’s No. 1 issue and says that after the bipartisan fiscal guardrails produced billions in surpluses used to pay down debt, the remainder should go back to towns as aid to cut property taxes or directly to taxpayers, faulting the current administration for spending it instead. On energy, he blames constrained natural-gas supply into New England, backs nuclear and tougher scrutiny of utility costs at PURA, and says the late-1990s deregulation of the energy market “has been a failure” and should be revisited. He cites state money he helped secure for Long Hill Green, the veterans center, Unity Park and Thrushwood Lake, plus firefighter cancer coverage, tax relief for volunteer firefighters and PTSD protections for first responders.

stories.headline: Masked crew rams a pickup through a Washington jewelry store in broad daylight — then flees empty-handed when the owner opens fire
stories.summary: A group of masked would-be thieves drove a white Toyota Tacoma through the front of Medina Jewelers in Lynnwood, Washington, shortly after 12:25 p.m. Tuesday and rushed inside, one of them apparently carrying an axe, according to police and surveillance video. The store owner grabbed a gun and fired, and the suspects ran out without taking anything, FOX13 Seattle reported; video shows a man believed to be the owner pointing the gun at them as they fled. Police said no one was hurt at the scene but it is unclear whether any suspect was struck, and they are still working to determine whether any of the suspects was armed. The video shows three vehicles circling the parking lot before the crash; the suspects escaped in a black BMW SUV, which hit a parked car and may have front passenger-side damage, and a silver Toyota or Infiniti sedan. “It was broad daylight and a pretty rare occurrence for us,” Lynnwood Police Cmdr. Joe Dickenson said. Detectives are asking tipsters to email crimetips@lynnwoodwa.gov referencing case No. 2026-37986.

stories.headline: American Airlines will put SpaceX’s Starlink Wi-Fi on every mainline jet — more than 1,000 planes — and keep it free for AAdvantage members
stories.summary: American Airlines said Thursday it will install SpaceX’s Starlink satellite Wi-Fi on every Airbus and Boeing jet in its mainline fleet, more than double the roughly 500 Airbus planes it planned to equip when it first announced the deal in May. Once installations are finished, more than 1,000 American jets are expected to have the faster service, and Wi-Fi is expected to stay free for members of its AAdvantage loyalty program. The Points Guy says the switch should especially help American’s long-haul Boeing 787s and 777s, many of which still use legacy Panasonic service with frequent connectivity gaps; only its regional jets are not slated for Starlink. “Dependable connectivity can make a meaningful difference in how they spend their time in the air,” chief customer officer Heather Garboden said. United, Alaska and Hawaiian already use or are installing Starlink, and Southwest and Frontier announced plans this year, while Delta and JetBlue are going with Amazon’s competing service, expected on Delta in 2028.

stories.headline: Def Leppard book a 45-date 2027 North American arena tour with Goo Goo Dolls and the Struts — including Pittsburgh, Madison Square Garden and Mohegan Sun
stories.summary: Def Leppard will tour North America next spring, with Goo Goo Dolls and the Struts joining a 45-date run that opens March 2, 2027, at the PPL Center in Allentown, Pennsylvania, and closes July 2 in Indianapolis. Stops near home include Newark’s Prudential Center on March 13, Boston’s TD Garden on March 17, Pittsburgh’s PPG Paints Arena on March 23, Madison Square Garden on June 23, Mohegan Sun Arena in Uncasville, Connecticut, on June 25 and Philadelphia on June 27. A fan club presale starts Monday, Oct. 12, at 10 a.m. local time, followed by Citi and Verizon presales at noon, with the general on-sale Friday, Oct. 16, at 10 a.m. local through Live Nation. The Sheffield hard rock band released a new single, “Rejoice,” early this year ahead of its latest Las Vegas residency, and guitarist Phil Collen has said the band is working on a new album expected in 2027.

stories.headline: Jets (1-3) come home to face the 3-1 Browns needing to fix their slow starts — Garrett Wilson: ‘we have to get on the board now’
stories.summary: The Jets return to MetLife Stadium on Sunday riding a three-game losing streak to host a Cleveland team that has won three straight since an opening-day blowout. Wide receiver Garrett Wilson, who leads the team with 24 catches, 270 yards and two touchdowns but was held to three catches in Chicago as the offense ran just 32 plays, said he feels a higher level of urgency: “We have to get on the board, we have to get on the board now.” The Jets have spotted their past three opponents early leads, scoring 17 first-half points in those games, while the Browns have been outscored 27-3 in first quarters; both teams have lived in one-score games, with the Jets losing to Green Bay in overtime and to Detroit and Cleveland beating Tampa Bay, Carolina and Pittsburgh by a combined 10 points. New York has been missing four offensive starters but could get tight end Mason Taylor back from a thumb injury, and Wilson called Browns cornerback Denzel Ward a player who “brings out the best in you.” It starts a nine-game run against AFC opponents, with three of the next four at home.

stories.headline: Indian’s CEO says he’s ‘disappointed’ Harley would ‘quit American bagger racing’ as the Motor Co. walks away from King of the Baggers
stories.summary: Indian Motorcycle CEO Mike Kennedy publicly criticized Harley-Davidson’s decision to leave MotoAmerica’s King of the Baggers, the bagger race series Harley helped found. “We are disappointed that Harley-Davidson would quit American bagger racing and walk away from something that has unified so many American V-twin riders regardless of which brand of motorcycle they ride,” Kennedy said, adding that “rivalry, and the inherent possibility of losing, is what makes competition truly meaningful.” He said Indian remains committed to MotoAmerica and the series. RideApart’s writer says he understood Harley’s cost-cutting logic at first, since the company is in a rebuilding phase and racing burns cash, but now sides with Kennedy, arguing Harley should have dropped its single-make MotoGP support series instead. The piece notes Harley is also courting younger riders with an upcoming entry-level bike, an expanded Revolution Max lineup, a returning Sportster and its purchase of EV dirt-bike brand Dust Moto, but warns it can’t leave its core bagger and cruiser buyers hanging.

stories.headline: LEGO’s $99.99 Marvel Skyline packs Avengers Tower, the Baxter Building, the Daily Bugle and a Galactus minifigure into a 1,261-piece microscale city
stories.summary: LEGO officially revealed The Marvel Skyline (67006) on Thursday, a 1,261-piece microscale display set due in January at $99.99, with pre-orders open now. The model lines up a who’s-who of Marvel addresses: the Daily Bugle, Avengers Tower, the Baxter Building, the Sanctum Sanctorum, the X-Mansion, Nelson and Murdock’s law office, the Department of Damage Control, Rand Enterprises, the Wakandan Embassy and Pym Laboratories, alongside villain strongholds such as Oscorp, Fisk Tower, Roxxon, Hammer Industries and A.I.M. It also includes microscale vehicles — the Avengers Quinjet, the X-Jet, a Thanos copter and the Leviathan — plus a Galactus minifigure and nanofigures of Spider-Man and the Human Torch. LEGO pitches it as adult-collector room decor and supports building it with family through the Build Together mode in its Builder app.

stories.headline: Penguins’ turnovers bury them in Washington: Capitals win 5-3 in Crosby-vs.-Ovechkin game No. 101 despite Bryan Rust’s goal in his season debut
stories.summary: The Penguins suffered their first loss of the season, 5-3 to the Capitals at Capital One Arena on Wednesday night, after opening 2-0. PensBurgh called it a game decided by self-inflicted mistakes. Washington scored on its first shot 23 seconds in, when Trevor van Riemsdyk’s turnover sprung Anthony Beauvillier on a breakaway; Bryan Rust, activated earlier in the day, answered 56 seconds later in his season debut, driving the net off a Ben Kindel feed. A Kris Letang reverse behind the net set up Tom Wilson’s goal, and in the second period a stray puck from goalie Arturs Silovs and a picked-off cross-ice pass by Declan Carlile led to goals by Pierre-Luc Dubois and Alex Tuch for a 4-1 Capitals lead. Pittsburgh clawed back on goals by Tommy Novak (on a Malkin rebound) and Nick Robertson’s tip, but Ryan Leonard restored the two-goal lead on a power play early in the third. Wilson finished with a goal and two assists. Pittsburgh outshot Washington 30-27; Silovs stopped 22 of 27 and Logan Thompson 27 of 30. Neither Sidney Crosby nor Alex Ovechkin registered a point. The Penguins play next in Columbus on Friday night.
